notes:
Summary: Mid-market fintech building client-facing analytics and fraud/risk reranking. Strong product fit for low-latency rerank + archive search, but unit economics don't hit their required thresholds. Finance/Procurement pushing back on minimum commit and projected GPU-backed serving costs. CTO likes Redwood's routing/caching approach; Head of Data/ML worried about token spend on long-context models.

Recent timeline (short):
- 2026-01-12: Intro call (Jordan AE) — use cases mapped (search + rerank + interactive chat). Good technical alignment.
- 2026-01-20: Security questionnaire sent (SE: Priya). Expect SOC2 + SSO + KMS.
- 2026-02-05: 2-week PoC started on hosted_api — rerank pipeline (100k queries simulated).
- 2026-02-19: PoC results reviewed — end-to-end latency OK (~110ms p50), but token and inference spend > internal target. PoC spend estimate extrapolated: ~$28k/mo for 100k qps pattern on hosted models.
- 2026-02-25: Pricing workshop with finance — asked for 12-mo commit options, lower committed GPUs and hybrid routing. Finance says minimum commit > budget.
- 2026-03-02: SE session on batching/quantization (notes in drive). Proposed 8-bit quantized endpoint saved ~30% in simulated throughput but still short of required $/req.
- 2026-03-10: Last outreach offering a short-term discounted pilot + 90-day evaluation. Silence since.

Key quotes / call notes: 
- CTO (M. Patel): "Architecture is ideal, but we cannot carry that level of recurring GPU spend until we see revenue uplift."
- Head of Data (L. Gomez): "If we can get a predictable dedicated tier with caching and lower token burn we'll re-evaluate."

POC findings (concise):
- Performance: latency and accuracy acceptable for reranking and chat flows.
- Economics: token-heavy prompts for long-context docs pushed per-interaction cost beyond their internal thresholds; dedicated GPU pricing with their required availability > what finance will approve without 6-12mo committed ARR.
- Workarounds explored: aggressive prefix caching, KV-cache reuse, quantization to int8, shorter context routing. Savings modeled: 25–40% but still leaves a gap.

Internal champion / org health: 
- Technical champion present (Head of Data) but not authorized to sign financial commit.
- Procurement/Finance is risk-averse post-Q4 hiring/IT freezes — high bar for multi-month GPU commitments.

Suggested next steps (tracked):
- Build an ROI model focused on fraud-prevention cost-savings (estimated reduction in chargebacks) and present blended pay-as-you-go + burst-dedicated option.
- Offer a 90-day staged pilot: low commit + overage credits, conditional extension if X reduction in fraud false positives.
- Provide a comparative TCO doc vs competitor proposals (OpenAI + self-hosted GPU).

Open items & blockers: 
- Procurement insists on a lower minimum commitment or a usage-capped contract.
- CFO requested full token-cost projection for Q3-Q4 at scale (missing: exact query growth forecast from customer).
- Security: need formal KMS integration demo in staging.

Current sentiment: Warm technically, cold financially. Risk: may pause and evaluate competitor proof that offers lower apparent token pricing at the cost of fewer features (e.g., smaller models or deferred caching).

Sales action: Track weekly for re-engagement; push updated price scenarios + ROI by 2026-03-20.
